::: {#rem-representation}

#### The same failure with people

A [training set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-training-set) with few eights is a small case of what [Ethics and Fairness](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/ethics.html#sec-bias-sources) in the DATA 471 notes calls representation bias:
a group that appears less often in the [training set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-training-set) can get less of the network's [accuracy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-accuracy).
Among [its documented cases](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/ethics.html#sec-documented-cases),
@buolamwini2018gender evaluated commercial face-analysis systems separately on groups of faces
and found [error rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-error-rate)s far higher for darker-skinned women than for lighter-skinned men;
the benchmarks that the systems' accuracy was usually reported on held mostly lighter-skinned faces.

:::
